page.layout: One page of verse, set as stanza-like lines in the centre; a marginal note "Swanenburgh" printed in black letter at the right beside line 5 of the verse; a catchword "Bercola" at the lower right; signature "Rr 3" at the foot.

p.i: Pervenit hunc rapido dexter ut amne bibat.
Hic novus & senior conjungunt Isala fauces
Iunior ast patulo digerit ore senem.
Iunior Ausonij nam dicitur Isala Drufi,
Isala sed senior tempore rarus aqua.
Quo veniat tandem,qui terminat omnia finis
Iunior in calamos Isala rursus eat.
Optima vix fluvius cernere castra valet.
Nam quatuor passus mille remota venit.
Bercola quam liquido Westphalus amne subit.
Pascua Spechusi primo sunt pervia fonti
Ad positum lardi nomen adepta domo.
Nomen ab Holthuso mutuat orbe lacus.
Hinc aliam vasto reficit fervore paludem,
Qua geminis nomen sumit inane molis.
Destinat in medio semita calle lacum.
Ad streperas amnem spectat abire rotas.
Bidrebeca tribus generet quod fontibus undam,
Vrbis id antiquæ confert insigne,quod illic
Triplicis in clypeo linea constet aquæ.

page.notes: The verse is printed as lines of a poem; the lines were joined into paragraphs here only because of the stanza layout. The margin note "Swanenburgh" is in black letter beside the fifth line. The lower right "Bercola" is a catchword. Some letters in the scan are faint and uncertain; the Latin is transcribed as printed with long s rendered as s.
